haiku-low.q1: Accepts the valid events; returns 202, listing rejected event_ids with reasons, only after the log durably writes every accepted event.
haiku-low.q2: Resends the same batch with the same event_ids, backing off exponentially from 1 s up to 5 minutes.
haiku-low.q3: The first copy in log order (lowest partition and offset) wins; later copies are dropped and kept only in the archive.
haiku-low.q4: Its received_at is 00:10 Tuesday, so it belongs to Tuesday's partition and Tuesday's replay. The client timestamp is never used.
haiku-low.q5: The existing key-value store holds event_id to partition:offset via atomic set-if-absent. Entries expire after an 8-day TTL.
haiku-low.q7: Offsets commit only after confirmed load; reprocessing re-emits the same winner, and a load id already in the load-log is skipped.
haiku-low.q8: It reads archived raw objects from D-8 through D+1. Rebuilt events go to staging, then atomically replace partition D.
haiku-low.q9: It reads archived raw copies from D-8 through D+1, keeps each event's lowest (partition, offset) copy, and keeps it only if received_at is in D.
haiku-low.q10: Partition D stays untouched and nothing is published. The lock is released and staging is kept. Operator fixes the cause and reruns replay(D), overwriting staging.
haiku-low.q11: Closed days with raw data still present for D-8 through D+1, so roughly up to 82 days old, and no replay of D already running.
haiku-low.q12: Undecided by Product; the plan does not choose. An isolated bot stage either drops suspected bots or keeps them with a flag.

sonnet.q1: It returns 202 listing each rejected event_id (or index if no usable id) with a reason; rejected events are not stored and the rest are accepted. It may return 202 only after the log confirms every accepted event is durably written (acks=all). If the whole batch is unparseable or has over 100 events, it returns 400 instead.
sonnet.q2: It resends the same batch with the same event_ids, backing off exponentially from 1 s up to 5 minutes; unacknowledged events are kept on device up to 7 days (mobile SDK).
sonnet.q3: The first copy in log order (lowest offset within the same partition) is the winner and goes to the warehouse; later copies are dropped live (kept only in the archive). Exception: if the first copy is over 8 days old (key expired), the later copy counts as new.
sonnet.q4: Tuesday's UTC day, because it is based on received_at (00:10 Tuesday), not the client timestamp. Tuesday's partition and Tuesday's replay.
sonnet.q5: In the existing key-value store (per-key TTL). Key is event_id, value is partition:offset of the winning copy, set atomically if absent. Entries are removed by the 8-day TTL.
sonnet.q6: NOT STATED for unreachability specifically. The document only covers the store losing state: duplicates leak into live partitions until affected days are replayed from the archive, and a fall in the dedup drop rate raises the alarm. Clients' events are still accepted by the collector and archived.
sonnet.q7: Each load has a deterministic id (partition plus start/end offset) recorded in a load-log table; a retried load whose id is already there is skipped. Offsets are committed only after the load is confirmed, so the batch is reprocessed and the same partition:offset in the key-value store means it is re-emitted as winner (no loss). Ideally the insert and load-log row commit in one warehouse transaction, but that is unconfirmed (open question), so a crash between them could still double-insert or skip a load.
sonnet.q8: Input: only raw objects from the archive in object storage for D-8 through D+1, as they exist at job start (not the log or key-value store). Output is built into a staging table/partition, never the live partition, before the atomic swap.
sonnet.q9: Over the whole window D-8..D+1, for each event_id it takes the copy with the lowest (partition, offset), the same rule as live (partition and offset are kept in the archive). It keeps the event for D only if that winning copy's received_at is in D. So a copy in D whose first copy arrived in D-3 is dropped; a first copy older than D-8 is outside the horizon, so the copy in D is treated as new.
sonnet.q10: Partition D is untouched (nothing published); the lock is released, the audit log records the failed check (for validation failure), and staging is kept for inspection. The operator fixes the cause and reruns replay(D), which overwrites staging; rerunning is safe.
sonnet.q11: Only closed days (D closed at 02:00 UTC on D+1 and the watermark passed the end of D), with raw data for D-8 through D+1 still existing (so D at most about 82 days old), and no replay already running for D.
sonnet.q12: Undecided by Product; the plan does not choose. There is an isolated bot stage between enrichment and load (and in replay). Option 1: drop suspected bots from events_clean. Option 2: keep them with an is_suspected_bot column. Either way raw retains bot events, and dedup runs before the bot stage.
